answer: Each identity claims one dune plot, self-prices it, and locks a 70-credit bond. A cedar post marks it, and anyone may buy it at the price. Its price stands by quill, open to all. Each epoch the owner pays 5% as tax; low prices invite buyouts, high prices bleed tax. A farm with 1,000 plots at 800 pays 40,000 tax per epoch and locks 70,000 bonds against a 40,000 pool. Reused cedar posts burn both bonds. An honest agent pays 40 and keeps its plot.
